{"query":"urllib3 GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw CVE-2026-97689 vulnerable function","follow_up_questions":null,"answer":null,"images":[],"results":[{"url":"https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-97689","title":"CVE-2026-97689: urllib3 Python Library DOS Vulnerability","content":"CVE-2026-97689 is a resource exhaustion vulnerability in urllib3, a widely used HTTP client library for Python. The flaw affects versions from 1.10.3 up to (but not including) 2.8.0. The HTTPResponse.read\_chunked and HTTPResponse.stream methods allocate unbounded memory when parsing chunked transfer-encoded responses. A malicious HTTP server can send a Transfer-Encoding: chunked response followed by a very long run of bytes with no newline, forcing the client to buffer indefinitely. The issue [...] The fix is committed in urllib3 commit cd770b0 and shipped in the urllib3 2.8.0 release. The patch introduces \_MAX\_CHUNK\_LINE\_LENGTH = 2\\16, matching http.client.\_MAXLINE, so the streaming path enforces the same bound as the standard library. Full advisory details are available in GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw.

### Workarounds [...] The defect resides in urllib3's streaming chunk parser inside src/urllib3/response.py. When a response uses Transfer-Encoding: chunked, the parser must read a chunk-size line terminated by CRLF before reading the chunk payload. The vulnerable implementation reads bytes until a newline or end-of-file without enforcing any maximum line length. A malicious upstream server can therefore stream an unbounded stream of non-newline bytes that the client buffers into memory.","score":0.8729662,"raw_content":null,"id":"12d7ea-00"},{"url":"https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2026-97689","title":"CVE-2026-97689 - Red Hat Customer Portal","content":"## Description

A flaw was found in urllib3. This flaw allows a Denial of Service (DoS) through unbounded memory allocation when parsing chunk-encoded responses. A malicious server can send an excessively long chunk-size line without a newline, exhausting client memory and terminating the application.
